title: Refraction & Snell's law
examples: What is the difference between reflection and refraction?
Does the speed of light change when it goes from air to water?
How do I use Snell's law to find an unknown angle?

explain.say: When light passes from one material to another it bends.

items: Air to glass: Light bends towards the normal.
Water to air: Light bends away from the normal.

explain.say: The bending of light is called refraction and it happens because of speed change.

draw.text: Refraction: Bending due to speed change.

explain.say: Snell's law relates the angles and the refractive indices of the two media.
The refractive index is the ratio of the sine of the incidence angle to the sine of the refraction angle.
A common example is light moving from air into water or glass.
If light moves from a slower medium to a faster one it bends away from the normal.

faq.q: What is the refractive index of a material?
faq.a: It is a number that tells us how much a material slows down light. It is often represented by the letter n.
asks: How do I find the refractive index?
What does n stand for in optics?

faq.q: Does light always bend when it enters a new material?
faq.a: Yes, unless the two materials have the same refractive index. If the speed does not change, there is no bending.
asks: Does light bend if the materials are the same?

faq.q: How do I calculate the angles using Snell's law?
faq.a: You must use the formula n equals the sine of the incidence angle divided by the sine of the refraction angle. Remember to use the correct units.
asks: What is the calculation for refraction?
Can I use trigonometry for this?

faq.q: Does the speed of light change in a vacuum?
faq.a: No, the speed of light in a vacuum is constant. This is why the refractive index is different for materials.
asks: Is the speed of light always the same?
What is the speed of light in empty space?

faq.q: If the angle of incidence is zero, what happens to the light?
faq.a: If the light hits the normal directly, the angle of refraction will also be zero. The light passes straight through.
asks: What if i is zero degrees?
Does the light bend if it hits straight on?

facts: Refraction is the bending of light as it passes between media.
Snell's law is mathematically expressed as n equals sine i divided by sine r.
The refractive index (n) relates to the speed of light in that material.
When light moves from air to glass, it generally bends towards the normal.

quiz.say: Light travels from air into glass. If the angle of incidence is forty degrees and the refractive index is one point five, what is the angle of refraction?
quiz.why: The formula shows that the ratio of sines equals the refractive index, allowing you to solve for the unknown angle.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the angle changes when the light passes into a new medium.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you cannot simply divide the angle by the refractive index value.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you must use the sine function on both sides of the equation.

quiz.say: If light moves from a slower medium to a faster medium, what happens to the angle?

options.show: It bends away from the normal.
options.say: It bends away from the normal.

options.show: The angle does not change at all.
options.say: The angle does not change at all.

quiz.why: When light speeds up, it bends away from the line perpendicular to the surface.

wrong.1: This happens when light slows down, not when it speeds up.
wrong.2: The angle changes unless the speed remains constant in both materials.
wrong.3: Reflection is bouncing off, while refraction is passing through and bending.

quiz.say: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between the angles?

options.show: The ratio of sines equals the refractive index.
options.say: The ratio of sines equals the refractive index.

options.show: The ratio of angles equals the refractive index.
options.say: The ratio of angles equals the refractive index.

options.show: The sine of the ratio equals the refractive index.
options.say: The sine of the ratio equals the refractive index.

options.show: The sine of the incidence angle equals the refractive index.
options.say: The sine of the incidence angle equals the refractive index.

quiz.why: This correctly states the mathematical relationship defined by Snell's law.

wrong.1: The law uses the sine of the angles, not the angles themselves.
wrong.2: The refractive index is the ratio of the sines, not the sine of the ratio.
wrong.3: This ignores the angle of refraction, which is necessary for the calculation.
